## 从未知操作识别点群: ## Identify a point group from unknown operations
[打开第 3 课](../#classroom/foundations?less: [Open Lesson 3](../#classroom/foundations?lesson=thirty-two) and expand the identification workshop. Make a prediction, then see how an operation transforms the three unit basis vectors. Reveal determinants, operation types, and counts as needed, and explain why each clue narrows the candidates. After checking your answer, open the matched group’s character table or three-dimensional operation lab.
工坊从 32 个代表空间群的完整线性部分取得精确分数坐标矩阵。选取的代表空间群都: The workshop takes exact fractional-coordinate matrices from the complete linear parts of 32 representative space groups. Each selected space group has point-group representatives with zero translational parts. Integer matrices supply the classification and orthonormal Cartesian matrices supply the visualization. The two matrices describe the same linear action in different bases. Their determinant, trace, and finite order are identical.
若 det R = +1，按 R 的有限阶给恒等或正旋转计数。若 det R =: For det R = +1, use the finite order of R to count the identity or a proper rotation. For det R = −1, use the order of −R to count rotoinversions. Order 1 of −R gives inversion, and order 2 gives reflection in a plane. The order of R alone groups inversion and reflection together as order 2 and groups threefold and sixfold rotoinversion together as order 6.
只看到一些操作时，每一类已见数量只给出下限。即使可见操作在乘法下封闭，仍可能是更: When you have seen only some operations, each observed count is a lower bound. Even an observed set that is closed under multiplication can be a subgroup of a larger point group. With a complete operation list, the count in every category must agree. The workshop checks for matches among the 32 ordinary crystallographic point-group types. Use the matrices to interpret a specific setting or axis direction. For actual structures with incomplete or noisy operations, use a structure symmetry analysis.
操作的国际记号和七个晶系内的 32 类可查阅 [International Ta: For the international notation and the 32 classes within seven crystal systems, see [International Tables for Crystallography, Section 3.2.1 and Table 3.2.1.1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/iucr/itc/Ac/ch3o2v0001/sec3o2o1/). For generating matrices, see [An introduction to crystal physics, Tables 2 and 3, IUCr](https://www.iucr.org/what-we-do/education/pamphlets/introduction-crystal-physics). The workshop uses the matrices in the site’s [BC space-group data](../data/space-groups.json) and [point-group atlas](../data/pointgroup-atlas.json).
